# Chapter 03 - The Next Case

The final meeting was quiet.

The board did not restore every name. It did not punish every liar. It removed three old explanations and left two protected omissions in place.

The accused archivist remained unnamed in the public conclusion.

The reviewer signed the protection note herself.

Another investigator added his name to the follow-up column because he had seen the missing twenty-seven minutes and could not pretend the gap was harmless.

At the end of the table, the protagonist's badge was moved from primary review to assisted observation.

No one called it punishment.

That made it harder to refuse.

"You can appeal," her colleague said.

"Appeal will not change the evidence."

She signed the adjustment form.

The pen paused after her name, leaving a small dark spot on the paper.

The next morning, a new body arrived without any old record attached.

The assistant reached for the intake pen and almost handed it to her first.

She looked at the first-contact line.

Her name was no longer there.

"You sign," she said. "I will observe."

Only after the assistant wrote the first line did she put on gloves and look at the body's wrist.
